Thesis: The Effect of a “glass ceiling” on the behavior and perception of children in high school
In this paper, we will present a research that focuses on the effect of a glass ceiling (the hypothesis) on the perception of students. In other words, we are interested to know if there is any relationship between the degree of a glass ceiling and student’s academic performance in college. We believe it can be said that the glass ceiling may not be the most effective way to achieve the goal of being academically competitive or more effective than a traditional teaching method. However, we will give some perspective on what is going on with the data from our research study. We believe that this study could help us to understand how much different kind of glass ceilings influences the perception of certain behaviors. It also shows that although a glass ceiling has been proven to have positive effects on students’ learning abilities, it does not have the same impact as a traditional teaching method.

A new approach to stop HIV transmission
(Nanowerk News) Scientists have developed a new way of detecting the presence of HIV in blood samples. The technique could help prevent the spread of the virus by preventing its replication inside cells that are infected with it.
In an article published in Science Translational Medicine, researchers report their results on how they used a different type of DNA called adenine to detect and track HIV using small proteins called microRNAs (miRNAs). In this study, the scientists used a single miRNA to detect the presence of HIV in human serum samples.
They found that targeting the microRNA targets resulted in significant reductions in viral load, which is the amount of particles that can enter the bloodstream. Viral loads decreased significantly when these miRNAs were targeted in the blood samples of people with AIDS who had undetectable levels of the virus.
"This approach could be used to determine if the antiretroviral treatment has been effective in individuals living with HIV infection," said Robert Lanza, PhD, a co-author of the paper and professor at the University of Maryland School of Medicine's Department of Immunology. The boiling point of water is 108.2 degrees Fahrenheit. It’s also called the “second best-sounding” gas. Water boils at a temperature ranging from 34 to 95 degrees F (40 to 70 Celsius).
Water boils at temperatures as low as -60 degrees F (-23 C), which means that it can boil for very long periods without freezing or boiling again. If you can control your heating and cooling system by lowering the temperature of the water, then you will be able to keep drinking water safe for longer periods without having to worry about its quality.
The boiling point of water varies depending on the amount of hydrogen in the air. At atmospheric pressure, it’s said to have a boiling point of -111.6 degrees Fahrenheit. This temperature is around 335 degrees Fahrenheit (0°C) at sea level. That’s why we call it an “atmospheric pressure.”
At lower altitudes, such as the Antarctic, the boiling point decreases rapidly – typically 35 to 100 degrees Fahrenheit per hour. For example, when people are camping, they may see more than 100 degrees Fahrenheit in the daytime.

You’ve probably heard of financial literacy before but it is not just about knowing how to calculate your income and assets. - Financial Literacy – What Is A Financial Literacy?
Financial literacy includes an overall understanding of how your money works, including how to save for the future, how to spend your money wisely and how to manage your money properly. The skills and knowledge required to make informed decisions in order to use your funds wisely include money management, budgeting and investing.
- Financial Literacy – Understanding Your Financial Goals And Values
Financial literacy involves being aware of your spending habits, as well as learning how to manage them with your money.
